turns.text: Before you begin: in your own words, what do you already know about "Reading a limestone cave"?
Limestone is a rock.
Which idea from earlier lessons do you expect to need most here, and why?
Explaining how long it takes.

Hi, I'm Dana. I'm a new volunteer guide who starts leading school tours next week and is worried about saying something wrong. I was told you can help me understand this. I really am starting from zero, so go slowly.
It fizzes with the acid so the wall is calcite limestone and slightly acidic water dissolves it slowly.
It is about two metres tall and at a growth rate of 0.1 mm a year that makes it roughly twenty thousand years old.
There are crinoid fossils and shells in the wall so this limestone formed on an ancient sea floor.
Here's something I don't understand yet: slightly, acidic and water. How would you explain it to me?
Stalactites are made of ice, frozen water I think.

Hold on. A moment ago you said something that sounded like "stalactites and stalagmites are made of ice or frozen water". If that were true, what would we expect to see? Does that match what you know?
I am not sure.
I'm lost. Could you try again with one concrete example?
I am not sure.
Go back to the course material you read before we started. Which part deals with slightly, acidic and water? What does it imply here?
I am not sure.
Oh! So does that mean caves are carved by fast flowing rivers cutting through the rock?
I am not sure.

Thank you. I think I could explain some of this to someone else now.

Not great.
